OK-governor.statusNote: Open seat, Gov. Stitt is term-limited. Former state Sen. Mike Mazzei defeated Attorney General Gentner Drummond by 2,020 votes out of more than 371,000 cast in the Aug 25 Republican runoff; Drummond conceded. House Minority Leader Cyndi Munson won the Democratic nomination June 16. Independents Jerry Griffin, Robert Brooks and Orlando Lynn Bush are also on the November ballot.

OK-senate.statusNote: Open seat: Sen. Markwayne Mullin resigned in March 2026 after his confirmation as Homeland Security secretary; appointed Sen. Alan Armstrong is not running. Rep. Kevin Hern won the June 16 Republican primary with 67.6% and no runoff. N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas defeated Jim Priest with 61% in the Aug 25 Democratic runoff. Independents Ron Meinhardt and Curtis Stinnett and Libertarian Sevier White are also on the November ballot; none of the three has documented policy positions we could find, so they appear by name only.

candidates.name: Gentner Drummond
candidates.background: Oklahoma Attorney General since 2023; former Air Force F-15 pilot who flew 32 combat missions in the Gulf War, Osage County rancher, banking lawyer, and principal owner of Blue Sky Bank. Led the June 16 primary with just over 25%, then lost the Aug 25 Republican runoff to Mike Mazzei by 2,020 votes and conceded.
priorities: Crack down on cartels and support law enforcement

cost.label: Would lower costs by confronting insurance companies and corporations rather than through broad tax cuts (News9 candidate guide)

immigration.label: 'Strong supporter of President Trump's border policies', tougher immigration enforcement and cooperation with federal authorities (News9 candidate guide)

taxes.label: 'Cut taxes responsibly without sacrificing schools, roads, or public safety', with property tax relief (campaign issues)

climate.label: Joined Republican AGs opposing the lesser prairie-chicken endangered listing and Biden administration changes to the 'waters of the United States' rule, and sued the EPA over ozone regulations (Wikipedia)

education.label: Education plan invests in public schools: reading proficiency by 3rd grade, CareerTech and apprenticeship expansion, incentivizing teachers (campaign issues)

safety.label: 'Crack down on cartel activity and drug trafficking' and 'support and strengthen local law enforcement' (campaign issues)

repro.label: As AG sued the Biden administration for suspending Oklahoma's Title X grant after the state declined to provide abortion referrals, defending the state's pro-life policies (Oklahoma AG press release)

democracy.label: In a DOJ voter-data settlement touted Oklahoma's proof-of-identity requirement, absentee ballot notarization, and ballot harvesting ban, pledging cooperation 'to eliminate voter fraud' (Oklahoma AG press release)

nullNotes.health: campaign healthcare plank is cost-focused (price transparency, rural hospital partnerships, holding insurers accountable) with no stance on public versus private coverage role; Ballotpedia and Wikipedia also empty on this axis; record search also empty (his AG letter calling Stitt's Medicaid managed care 'an abject, systemic failure' is an operational critique that also disparages Obamacare, not a coverage-role stance)
nullNotes.housing: checked campaign issues page, Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, News9 candidate guide; property tax relief is his only housing-adjacent item and it does not fit the axis; record search also empty (his OHFA letter concerns appointee removal, not housing policy)

candidates.name: Mike Mazzei
candidates.now: Chairman and CEO, Trinity Strategic Wealth (Tulsa)
candidates.background: Former state senator for the Bixby area (2004-2016) who chaired the Senate Finance Committee, and Gov. Stitt's first Secretary of Budget. Founder of a Tulsa financial planning firm. Won the Aug 25 Republican runoff over Attorney General Gentner Drummond by 2,020 votes out of more than 371,000 cast, after advancing with just over 25% on June 16; endorsed by President Trump per his campaign site.
priorities: Eliminate the state income tax in phases
Lower the cost of living for families

cost.label: 'Lower the cost of living for families' by cutting taxes and making government live within its means (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Pledges prosecuting criminals and deporting undocumented immigrants, plus stronger action against cartels and foreign influence (KOSU)

taxes.label: Three-phase plan to eliminate the state income tax, starting with a cut from 4.75% to 3.25%; calls the tax code 'a giant octopus' (KOSU)

education.label: Mixed: up to $150 million for phonics-based reading programs and a statewide literacy director, while vowing to remove 'woke ideology' from classrooms (KOSU)

safety.label: Targets 'Mexican cartels and illegal marijuana operations' as top public safety priorities (News9 candidate guide)

repro.label: 'Life begins at conception'; opposes abortion in all circumstances (campaign issues)

nullNotes.health: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no healthcare stance documented; record search also empty (no roll calls from his 2004-2016 Senate service surfaced in fetched sources)
nullNotes.housing: his 'no Oklahoman should be taxed out of their home' plank is senior and veteran property tax relief, not a build-versus-protect housing stance; checked campaign site, KOSU, Ballotpedia; record search also empty
nullNotes.climate: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no energy or climate stance documented; record search also empty (Wikipedia and Ballotpedia list no energy votes from his Senate service)
nullNotes.democracy: checked campaign issues page, KOSU launch coverage, Ballotpedia, News9 candidate guide; no election-law stance documented; record search also empty (his individual vote on Oklahoma's 2009 voter ID referral could not be documented in any fetched source)

candidates.name: Cyndi Munson
candidates.background: Oklahoma House minority leader and the first Asian American elected to the Oklahoma Legislature; daughter of a Vietnam veteran and a South Korean immigrant mother, and a first-generation college graduate. Worked in nonprofits before winning her Oklahoma City House seat in 2015. Won the June 16 Democratic primary with 75.1%.
priorities: Public school funding and teacher raises
Lower healthcare and prescription drug costs
Let voters repeal the abortion ban

health.label: Backs Oklahoma's voter-approved Medicaid expansion covering roughly 200,000 working Oklahomans; would cut drug and premium costs (KOSU)

immigration.label: As House minority leader opposed HB 4156 making unlawful presence a state crime, calling it 'extremist legislation' offering 'false hope and false solutions' (Oklahoma Voice)

education.label: Bring public school funding over the regional average, raise pay for public school teachers and staff, and end the voucher program sending public dollars to private schools (campaign priorities)

safety.label: Emphasizes 'prevention and addressing root causes of crime' through mental health services (News9 candidate guide)

repro.label: Would 'send the repeal of the abortion ban to a vote of the people' (campaign priorities)

nullNotes.cost: her affordability record is the grocery-tax repeal she championed plus unspecified healthcare cost reductions; targeted tax relief without an intervene-or-deregulate mechanism does not fit this axis (checked campaign priorities, KOSU profile, News9 guide); record search also empty

nullNotes.taxes: supports 'targeted tax relief for working families' and expanded credits rather than broad cuts or raising taxes on corporations; per calibration, targeted household tax cuts do not fit the axis (News9, campaign priorities); record search also empty (she debated against the 2025 income tax cut while calling for targeted relief protecting the revenue base, still off-axis)

nullNotes.democracy: checked campaign priorities page, KOSU profile, News9 candidate guide; nothing documented; record search also empty (her State of the State response comment on ballot measures is incidental)

candidates.name: Kevin Hern

sources.label: News9: Hern wins the June 16 GOP Senate primary with 67.6%
NonDoc: Hern launches U.S. Senate campaign

candidates.now: U.S. Representative, OK-1; chair, House Republican Policy Committee
candidates.background: Longtime Tulsa-area McDonald's franchisee who built and sold a group of restaurants before winning the 1st District House seat in 2018; chaired the Republican Study Committee and now chairs the House Republican Policy Committee. Gave up his House seat to run for Senate after Markwayne Mullin resigned to lead DHS, framing his campaign as ensuring 'President Trump has a loyal ally.' Won the June 16 Republican primary with 67.6%, avoiding a runoff; endorsed by President Trump.
priorities: America First loyalty to President Trump's agenda
Balanced federal budget and spending cuts

cost.label: Chaired the Republican Study Committee budget that frames deregulation and $16 trillion in spending cuts as the fix for inflation and high prices (RSC FY24 budget, Hern's House site)

health.label: Supports repealing the Affordable Care Act in favor of free-market health care that 'lowers costs' with decisions between patients and doctors (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Voted for H.R. 695 to fund the border wall and cosponsored H.R. 768 to defund sanctuary campuses (campaign site)

taxes.label: Voted yes on final passage of H.R. 1, the July 2025 reconciliation law making the 2017 tax cuts permanent (House Clerk roll call 190)

climate.label: 'We have an ambitious goal of not only energy independence, but energy dominance': backs all-of-the-above production including oil and gas (Hern House press release)

education.label: Introduced the Student Empowerment Act with Sen. Cruz to extend 529 accounts to private, religious and homeschool K-12 expenses, 'giving students and families the freedom to choose' (Hern House press release)

repro.label: Says 'all life is sacred and begins at conception' and positions himself as a pro-life advocate (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Voted to sustain the objection to counting Pennsylvania's 2020 electoral votes on Jan 7, 2021 (House Clerk roll call 11)

nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia, hernforsenate.com, NonDoc campaign launch coverage and House press releases; no housing position documented
nullNotes.safety: checked Ballotpedia, hernforsenate.com and NonDoc launch coverage; Second Amendment items do not map to this axis and no policing or sentencing position was documented

candidates.name: N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas

sources.label: KSLA: Thomas wins the Aug 25 Democratic runoff with 61%
NonDoc: Thomas wins the runoff, first democratic socialist nominee

candidates.now: Registered nurse and community health worker
candidates.background: A 31-year-old nurse from Ardmore, Chickasaw Nation citizen and military spouse, and a political newcomer who identifies as a democratic socialist. Led the five-way June primary with about 45%, then defeated attorney Jim Priest with 61% in the Aug 25 runoff to become the Democratic nominee. Says she would push to impeach President Trump in her first 100 days.
priorities: A living wage and price gouging protections
Public school funding and teacher pay

cost.label: Platform calls for 'a living wage minimum wage' and 'strong price gouging protections' (campaign policies page)

health.label: Aims for a single-payer 'Medicare for all' system and funding rural hospitals (NonDoc runoff profile)

housing.label: Backs investment in affordable housing, emergency housing and utility relief, and 'accountability for predatory landlords' (campaign policies page)

taxes.label: Supports tax reform that benefits working families rather than the wealthy (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey)

climate.label: Would invest in renewable energy and sustainable practices to address increasingly severe natural disasters (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey)

education.label: Platform: competitive teacher pay, fully fund special education, free school breakfast and lunch, smaller class sizes (campaign policies page)

safety.label: Would mandate trauma-informed training for law enforcement and protect survivors from criminalization for self-defense (campaign policies page)

repro.label: Platform: 'Restore Roe v. Wade federally' and protect women from prosecution over miscarriage or pregnancy complications (campaign policies page)

democracy.label: Platform: safeguard voting access for disabled Americans (campaign policies page)

nullNotes.immigration: checked jasmineforok.com policies page, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, and NonDoc primary and runoff coverage; no immigration or ICE position documented in any fetched source
